G8000.definition:
1. a thunderbolt , Lat. fulmen, (Homer), etc.: generally, thunder :—;but thunder  properly was βροντή, Lat. tonitru; lightning was στεροπή, Lat. fulgur. 
2. metaphorically, κεραυνὸν ἐν γλώσσῃ φέρειν, of Pericles, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8001.definition: to strike with thunderbolts , (Herdotus Historicus):—; Pass., κεραυνωθείς (Hesiod), etc. (ML)

G8002.definition: the tail  of a beast, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G8003.definition:
1. the Cercopes  were a kind of men-monkeys , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. metaphorically a mischievous fellow, knave , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8006.definition:
to stain, sully, soil , (Euripides) 
from κηλί_ς (ML)

G8007.definition: 1. a muzzle , put on a led horse, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8012.definition: to mix  wine with water, in 3rd singular imperfect ἐκίρνα and κίρνη, participle κιρνάς, (Odyssey by Homer); in (Herdotus Historicus), 3rd singular present κιρνᾶι, 1st plural κίρναμεν. (ML)

G8013.definition: to crave for strange food , of pregnant women: metaphorically, κ. τῆς εἰρήνης (Aristophanes Comicus); with infinitive to long  to do a thing, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8015.definition:
1. a pillar , Lat. columna, (Odyssey by Homer): a flogging-post , (Sophocles Tragicus); proverbial, ἔσθιε τοὺς Μεγακλέους κίονας eat the pillars  of his hall, for being a spendthrift, he had nothing else left to give, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. in plural the pillars guarded by Atlas , which keep heaven and earth asunder, (Odyssey by Homer); whereas in (Herdotus Historicus) Mount Atlas  is ὁ κίων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ. 
3. a columnar grave-stone , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8017.definition: a bar  for closing a door, (Homeric Hymns):—;mostly in plural, like Lat. claustra, [variant datesTragica Adespota, etc. (ML)

G8020.definition: Diminutive of κλῆμα:—;in plural brush-wood, fagot-wood , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8024.definition:
the round of a ladder , (Euripides) 
from κλῖμαξ (ML)

G8025.definition:
1. a ladder  or staircase  (because of its leaning aslant) , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; a scaling-ladder , (Thucydides); κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις (Aeschulus Tragicus):—; a ship's ladder , (Euripides) 
2. a frame with cross-bars , on which persons to be tortured were tied, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. in (Sophocles Tragicus), κλίμακες ἀμφίπλεκτοι intertwining ladders , to express the entanglement  of the limbs of wrestlers. 
4. a climax , i. e. a gradual ascent from weaker expressions to stronger, Lat. gradatio, as Cicero's abiit, evasit, erupit.  (ML)

G8027.definition:
1. a dog-collar , especially a large wooden collar , put on mischievous dogs, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a  sort of pillory , (Euripides) 
3. χρύσεος κλ. a collar  of gold, [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8029.definition: to twist by spinning, spin , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., τὰ κλωσθέντα one's destiny , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8033.definition: the part between the knee and ankle, the leg , Lat. tibia, (Homer), etc. (ML)

G8034.definition: a greave  or piece of armour from knee to ankle , Lat. ocrea, περὶ κνήμῃσιν ἔθηκεν (Iliad by Homer); the κνημῖδες were fastened at the ankle with clasps  ἐπισφύρια);  βόειαι κνημῖδες are ox-hide leggings , used by labourers, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8036.definition: a nettle , Lat. urtica, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8037.definition:
1. to scrape  or grate: to tickle : metaphorically, of love, to nettle, chafe, irritate , (Herdotus Historicus); of satiety, (Pindar); of anxiety, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; οὐ κνίσω τὸ ῥῆμ᾽ ἕκαστον will  not attack  every word, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., κνίζεσθαί τινος to be stung  (with love) for  one, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. κν. ὀργάν to provoke  anger, (Pindar) (ML)

G8038.definition: a hollow, deep valley , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8040.definition:
1. hollow, hollowed , epithet of ships, which in early times were hollowed out of trees, (Homer); later, κοίλη ναῦς was the hold  of the ship, (Herdotus Historicus); so, ἡ κοίλη alone, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;of the Trojan horse, κ. λόχος, κ. δόρυ (Odyssey by Homer); κ. κάπετος, of a grave, (Iliad by Homer); κ. δέμνια, of the bed when no one is in it , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. of Places, lying in a hollow  or forming a hollow , κοίλη Λακεδαίμων the vale  of L., (Odyssey by Homer); κ. Θεσσαλία (Herdotus Historicus); κ. Ἄργος (Sophocles Tragicus); τὰ Κοῖλα τῆς Εὐβοίας (Herdotus Historicus); ἡ Κοιλή the valley  of the Ilissus, (Herdotus Historicus):—; κ. λιμήν of a harbour lying between high cliffs , (Odyssey by Homer); κ. αἰγιαλός an embayed  beach, (Odyssey by Homer):—; κ. ὁδός a hollow  way, (Iliad by Homer):—; κ. ποταμός a river nearly empty  of water, (Thucydides) (so Virgil, cava flumina) : metaphorically of the voice, hollow , μυκάσατο κοῖλον (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); φθέγγεσθαι κοῖλον (Lucian) 
3. as Substantive κοῖλον, ου, τό, a hollow, cavity, ravine , (Plato Philosophus); like κοιλία, of the cavities  in the body, τὰ κ. γαστρός (Euripides); also, ἐν τῷ κοίλῳ καὶ μυχῷ τοῦ λιμένος (Thucydides) (ML)

G8043.definition: a hollow, cavity , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor), etc. (ML)

G8044.definition:
1. to put to sleep , (Euripides); ἄημα ἐκοίμισε πόντον, i. e. the winds suffer  the sea to rest—;  by ceasing (cf. Virg. straverunt aequora venti) , (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically, μεγαληγορίαν κ. to lay  pride asleep , (Euripides); so, κ. τὰς λύπας (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass., παῖς κοιμίζεται (Euripides) 
2. of the sleep of death, (Sophocles Tragicus); also in Mid., (Euripides) (ML)

G8045.definition: to put to bed :—;Mid., doric aor1 ἐκοιταξάμην, to go to bed, sleep , (Pindar) (ML)

G8048.definition: to flatter , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—; Pass. to be flattered, be open to flattery , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8050.definition:
1. of birds, to peck at , [Refs 2nd c.AD, variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;of Pegasus, to strike  the ground with his hoof, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. to carve  or chisel , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8062.definition:
1. dust, a cloud of dust , stirred up by men's feet, (Iliad by Homer); also in plural, like Lat. arenae, (Homer), etc. 
2. sand  or soil  (see. ὑπερέπτω); (Iliad by Homer) 
3. ashes , in plural like Lat. cineres, (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. a fine powder , sprinkled over wrestlers' bodies after being oiled, to make them more easily grasped by the opponent:—;this powder was also used in the bath, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 ι- in κονίῃσιν, in other cases ι- usually. (ML)

G8064.definition: a pole, punting-pole, boat-hook , Lat. contus, (Odyssey by Homer), attic: the shaft  of a pike, (Lucian) (ML)

G8065.definition: a strong-smelling plant, fleabane, pulicaria , poetry κνύζα, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8068.definition:
1. dung, ordure, manure , (Homer), etc. 
2. a farm-yard, home-stead , (Homer) (ML)

G8070.definition:
1. feminine of κόρος, κοῦρος 
2. a maiden, maid, damsel , Lat. puella, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
3. a bride, young wife , (Homer) 
4. a daughter , κοῦραι Διός (Iliad by Homer); κ. Διός, of Athene, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;in vocative, κούρα my daughter , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. the pupil  of the eye, Lat. pupula, because a little image appears therein, (Euripides) 
6. a long sleeve  reaching over the hand, (Xenophon Historicus) 
7. Κόρη, doric Κόρα, ionic Κούρη, ἡ, Cora, the Daughter  (of Demeter), name under which Persephone (Proserpine) was worshipped in Attica, τῇ Μητρὶ καὶ τῇ Κούρῃ (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; Δημήτηρ καὶ Κόρη (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8072.definition:
a club, mace , (Iliad by Homer):—; a shepherd's staff , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
 ῦ in (Homer); υ_ in (Euripides) (ML)

G8073.definition:
1. the head, top, highest point;  hence, 
2. the crown  or top of the head , (Iliad by Homer), attic 
3. the top  or peak  of a mountain, (Iliad by Homer) 
4. metaphorically the highest point , Lat. summa, παντὸς ἔχει κορυφάν is the best of all , (Pindar); κορυφὰ λόγων προτέρων the sum and substance  of ancient legends, (Pindar) 
5. the height  or excellence of  a thing, i. e. the choicest, noblest, best , (Pindar) 
 (ML)

G8074.definition:
1. Lat. cornix, the chough or sea-crow , a small kind with red legs and bill, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. = κόραξ, the carrion-crow , (Hesiod) 
3. anything hooked  or curved , like a crow's bill, 
4. the handle on a door , (Odyssey by Homer) 
5. the tip of a bow , on which the bowstring was hooked, (Homer):—;metaphorically, βιῷ κορώνην ἐπιθεῖναι to put a finish  to life, (Lucian) (ML)

G8077.definition:
1. a cup , (Homer) 
2. the cup  or socket  of a joint, especially of the hip-joint, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. a liquid measure , containing 6 κύαθοι, i. e. nearly half a pint , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8078.definition:
1. a shearing  or cropping  of the hair, tonsure , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a lock cut off , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8079.definition: a barber, hair-cutter , Lat. tonsor, [5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina, etc. (ML)

G8080.definition:
1. light, nimble , [variant datesTragica Adespota; used by (Homer) only in neuter plural as. adverb κοῦφα προβιβάς stepping lightly on, (Iliad by Homer):—;metaphorically, κουφότεραι φρένες too buoyant , (Pindar) 
2. metaphorically also light, easy , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. empty, unsubstantial, vain , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. light  in point of weight, opposite to βαρύς, (Plato Philosophus), etc.; κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνωθε πέσοι may earth lie lightly  on thee, sit tibi terra levis , (Euripides); of soldiers, ὡπλισμένοι κουφοτέροις ὅπλοις (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. adverb -φως, lightly, nimbly , (Aeschulus Tragicus); κ. ἐσκευασμένοι, of soldiers, (Thucydides) 
6. metaphorically lightly, with light heart , κουφότερόν μετεφώνεε (Odyssey by Homer); κούφως φέρειν to bear lightly , (Euripides); ὡς κουφότατα φέρειν (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. lightly, with ease , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8083.definition: only in present, to have a sick head-ache , consequent upon a debauch, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8089.definition:
1. a mixing vessel , especially a large bowl, in which the wine was mixed with water , and from which the cups were filled, (Homer), etc.; οἶνον δ᾽ ἐκ κρητῆρος ἀφυσσάμενοι δεπάεσσιν ἔκχεον (Iliad by Homer); πίνοντες κρητῆρας drinking bowls of wine , (Iliad by Homer); κρητῆρα στήσασθαι ἐλεύθερον to give a bowl of wine  to be drunk in honour of the deliverance, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπιστέψασθαι ποτοῖο, see. ἐπιστέφω. 
2. metaphorically, κρατῆρα πλήσας κακῶν having filled a bowl  full of woes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. any cup-shaped hollow, a basin  in a rock, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8090.definition: a flesh-hook , to take meat out of the pot, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8091.definition: to distribute flesh, to divide the flesh  of a victim among the guests, (Lucian):—;Mid. to divide among themselves , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8092.definition: hung, hung up, hanging , κρ. αὐχένος hung by  the neck, (Sophocles Tragicus); with genitive, also, hung from  or on  a thing, (Euripides): —; κρεμαστὴ ἀρτάνη, i. e. a halter, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, βρόχοι κρ. (Euripides) (ML)

G8093.definition: a well, spring, fountain , Lat. fons, (Homer), etc.; opposite to φρέαρ (a tank), (Herdotus Historicus): —;Poets use it in plural for water , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8094.definition:
1. a half-boot , (Xenophon Historicus):—; κρηπῖδες soldiers' boots , i. e. soldiers  themselves, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. generally, a groundwork, foundation, basement  of a temple or altar, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;metaphorically, κρηπὶς σοφῶν ἐπέων (Pindar); οὐδέπω κρηπὶς κακῶν ὕπεστι we have not yet got to the bottom  of misery, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ ἐγκράτεια ἀρετῆς κρηπίς self-control is the foundation  of virtue, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. the walled edge  of a river, a quay , Lat. crepido, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8095.definition:
1. a ring  on a horse's breast-band, to fasten it to the peg  ἕστωρ); at the end of the carriage-pole, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. an eyelet-hole  in sails, through which the reefing-ropes were drawn, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8096.definition:
1. a ram , Lat. aries, (Homer), etc. 
2. a battering-ram , Lat. aries, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8097.definition:
1. the thread which is passed between the threads of the warp  στήμων, tela ), the woof  or weft , Lat. subtemen, (Hesiod), etc. 
2. κροκύς, the flock  or nap of woollen cloth, cloth with curly nap , (Aristophanes Comicus): in plural, μαλακαῖς κρόκαις with cloths of  soft wool , (Pindar); κρόκαισι with flocks of wool , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8098.definition:
1. a lizard , properly an ionic word, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. the Nile-lizard, crocodile , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8099.definition:
1. the crocus , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. saffron  (which is made from its stigmas), (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)
